walkthroughs.body_html:
Reactants on the left, products on the right.

Peak height above reactants = activation energy.

Net difference = enthalpy change.

Catalyst lowers Ea by providing an alternative pathway.

It does not change delta H.

Equilibrium position is unchanged.

Increase reactant concentration -> shifts towards products.

Increase temperature -> shifts in endothermic direction.

Increase pressure -> shifts towards fewer gas moles.

options: delta H
activation energy
position of equilibrium
yield at equilibrium

mcqs.q: Which factor does not affect rate?
options: temperature
concentration
colour of beaker
surface area

mcqs.q: How does a catalyst speed up a reaction?
options: A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.
A catalyst lowers the activation energy of the original reaction pathway.
It provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.

mcqs.q: Does a catalyst affect the position of equilibrium?
options: A catalyst shifts the equilibrium towards the products.
No — it speeds up both the forward and reverse reactions equally, so equilibrium is reached faster but at the same position.
A catalyst increases the yield by being consumed in the forward reaction only.
The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.

mcqs.q: In an exothermic reaction, what happens energetically with the bonds?
options: Bond breaking releases energy and bond making absorbs energy.
The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.
Energy released forming new bonds exceeds energy absorbed breaking existing bonds.
A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
